institutionName: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
The university was important to me, I chose an University where I could take some classes that I found both interesting but also relevant for the direction I want to go with my education 
I also chose Tromsø because of the location and nature, I have previously taken courses involving the Arctic climate and Arctic organisms, so it was a great environment for me to study in

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I it hard not to be affected by the situation with covid, that got worse during my stay, but I do think I still got a lot out of my stay, but especially before restrictions and zoom

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I was quite easy, we got a lot of information well ahead of semester start, so that was nice, sometimes I had to wait a bit long for a respons on mail, but overall it was very nice

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had an introduction meeting which was very informative, then I got a "buddy" (an older student) whom I could ask questions, but most of all I just asked my fellow students

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: As mentioned we had a the info meeting on zoom, there was also a very nice welcoming week planned

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was alright, I think we got a bit lucky with our housening, but I still think it was a lot easier than to get student housing, cause there is not enough student housing for everyone (or at least it does not seem like it)

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You miss out of some social activities, when you are not living in a student housing, so I regret that about not doing student housing. On the other hand we got a lot more out of our money, we lived five people in a 2 floor house, and it was of course more expensive, but not that much more

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I got lucky, but it is my clear impression that it is very hard to get student housing if you don't apply months ahead

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was fine

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was just a lot of sending emails back and forth, and sometimes I had to wait a long time, probably also due to the fact that it was summer holiday, so that was sometimes a bit stressful

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I called both KU and UiT for help, and got a lot of help from both

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: There is not a lot of classes if you are a bachelor student, so that was a bit problematic, I ended up with getting a master course, but that was also great

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It was pretty straightforward, so I don't recall having any good advice

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found them interesting, I had both an excursion week and a lab week, so it was nice that they combine classroom teaching with practical teaching

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found the level suiting

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of versatile teaching, including excursions, debates, seminars and such, which I only experienced in a few of my classes on UCPH

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
An introduction to fish biology 
Biologiske ressurser i Nord 
Arctic Marine Pollution

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all three of them, I am very pleased with the choice I made

questions.answer: Everything is just more expensive in Norway, so I've used more money than I expected to

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Beers are quite expensive ;) and some vegetables

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a lot, swimming, skiing, dancing, sailing etc etc

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed swimming and sailing myself, but I think there is a lot of great opportunities and at student prices

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hiking, skiing, bird and whale watching from land

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy as the danish and norwegian cultures are quite alike

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Get them a beer, then the Norwegians are more social

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not any really

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their love for winter sports and the language

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: To attend the welcoming week, to pick classes with excursions (there are quite a few), and to try to explore as much of the nature as possible

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be prepared for the dark time, it can be quite hard to live in a place with limited day light. I normally cope with danish winter darkness just fine, but I found it very challenging to adjust to limited and in the end no sunlight, so also remember to take vitamin D starting in September

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: My living situation, I lived in a house with 4 different nationalities, so I got really close with some people that are different than myself. I also enjoyed the University very much

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To settle in in a foreign country and the limited day light

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
